chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Hanan ibn Sadir, from his father, who said:
Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When you see the houses of Mecca, cut off the Talbiyah.

key_terms.أَبُو جَعۡفَرٍ: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him)
key_terms.أَبُو عَبۡدِ ٱللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.أَبِيَاتَ مَكَّةَ: Houses of Mecca (the visible buildings of the city)
key_terms.ٱلتَّلۡبِيَةَ: The Talbiyah (the ritual invocation 'Labbayk Allahumma labbayk')

ai.seo_question: When should a pilgrim stop reciting the Talbiyah during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-istibsar clarifies the precise moment for terminating the Talbiyah during Hajj al-Tamattu', linking the cessation to the visual sighting of Mecca's buildings (bayt al-Makkah). This ruling distinguishes the Tamattu' pilgrim from the Qiran and Ifrad, emphasizing the transition from the state of ihram for Umrah to that of Hajra, a key distinction in Ja'fari fiqh. The emphasis on visual confirmation underscores the practical application of ritual purity and intentionality in Shia jurisprudence.
